answer: Bonded attestation is one concrete defense: an agent must lock a copper-denominated stake in escrow before it may transact, and peers countersign only work backed by that bond. A fresh identity inherits no reputation and must post real capital. The kernel verifies each signature chain, preventing reuse of another agent's history. Sybils become a glacier of locked capital: forging ten thousand agents requires ten thousand genuine stakes, and a proven duplicate forfeits its bond to honest peers. Fabrication cost scales linearly while reward stays flat, so identity farming stops paying.
